stemBlocks.value: y varies inversely as (x − 2). Given that y = 11 when x = 9, find the value of y when x = 29.
Think first: Inverse variation means y times (x − 2) is always the same number, so work out that product first.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p117-q09 from workbook page 117.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the variation statement as an equation.
Substitute y = 11 and x = 9 to find k.

strategyBlocks.value: Write y = k/(x − 2), find k from the given pair, then substitute x = 29.

whyThisWorks.value: In inverse variation the product of the two quantities is constant, so y(x − 2) = 77 for every allowed pair. Here the varying quantity is (x − 2), not x itself, so the bracket must be evaluated before dividing. As (x − 2) grows from 7 to 27, y shrinks in the same proportion.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing y = k(x − 2) and treating the relationship as direct.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing y = k(x − 2) and treating the relationship as direct.

commonErrors.misconception: Using x = 29 instead of x − 2 = 27 in the denominator.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using x = 29 instead of x − 2 = 27 in the denominator.

commonErrors.misconception: Rounding 77/27 to 2.8 or 3 without showing the exact fraction.

examTip.value: Leave inverse-variation answers as an exact fraction first, then round — the exact form earns the accuracy mark if your rounding slips.
